requirements.evidence: Migrations, models, enum, factories, policies and the docs edit are all present, but several contract items are unusable: app/Models/Entity.php:6 imports a non-existent `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\SoftDeletes` trait, app/Models/User.php:56-61 is a PHP parse error, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:11 redeclares `use App\Models\UserRole;` (fatal), and the SQLite migration never creates the required stored generated column (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:29-40), so the one-owner invariant is not enforced there. Policy comparisons against enum casts (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:24,36) are always false, so update/delete/manageSettings/assignRole do not behave as specified.

conventions.evidence: No tests at all, against the mandatory test-first rule (conventions.md:12-21); no CHANGELOG entry (conventions.md:103); migrations are hand-written named classes rather than generated anonymous-class migrations with raw SQL mixed in (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:7-8); policies are registered twice (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:35-36 and a new app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php); docblock in app/Models/UserRole.php:13 contradicts the owner-only settings rule.

security.evidence: Owner protection in app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:26 compares an enum-cast role with a string (`$membership->role === UserRole::Owner->value`), so it is always false and execution falls through to the self-removal branch at :31, letting the owner delete their own owner membership. Roles are checked with `in_array($membership->role, [...->value])` in app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:20 and app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:24, which is always false, so authorization results are unreliable. No validation/escaping issues because no input or views are added; $fillable is deliberate.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all (no tests/ additions), so none of the migrations, models, factories, owner invariant or policy matrix is covered; conventions require a Pest/PHPUnit test for every implemented piece including authorization paths.

simplicity.evidence: The owner invariant is implemented twice-over with a plain column plus two hand-written triggers (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:29-43) instead of the platform's generated column feature, and policy registration is duplicated between app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:35-36 and the unused app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php. Redundant same-namespace imports and unused imports in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:7-10 add noise.

readability.evidence: Dead, duplicated block after app/Models/User.php:56-61 and duplicate imports in app/Models/EntityMembership.php:7-11 look like an editing accident; app/Models/UserRole.php:13 documents `manageable()` as 'roles that can manage settings ... (i.e., non-owner roles)' which is the opposite of the domain rule; AppServiceProvider imports classes it then references by FQCN.

scope.evidence: All added files serve the requested data model/authorization task. Minor extras: an unnecessary second policy provider (app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php) and an unrelated editorial change removing 'billing only for owner' from docs/database-schema.md:138.

issues.explanation: A stray `{ return ['email_verified_at' => ..., 'password' => ...]; }` block was left after `membershipFor()`, which is a PHP parse error ('unexpected token "{"') and prevents the User model, and therefore the application, from loading.
`use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\SoftDeletes;` is not the SoftDeletes trait, so `use HasFactory, SoftDeletes;` at line 13 fails and the Entity model cannot be instantiated.
`use App\Models\UserRole;` is declared twice (lines 7 and 11), which is a PHP fatal error ('Cannot use ... because the name is already in use') and makes the membership model unloadable.

The SQLite branch does not create the required stored generated `owner_seq` column (it adds a plain INTEGER column plus triggers), and Laravel's `DB::statement` prepares only the first of the two concatenated CREATE TRIGGER statements, so the INSERT trigger is silently never created and `owner_seq` stays NULL on insert; the unique index therefore accepts a second owner, breaking the core invariant.

Because `role` is cast to `UserRole`, the owner guard `$membership->role === UserRole::Owner->value` is always false, so an owner can fall through to the self-removal branch and delete their own owner membership, which the task explicitly forbids.

Role checks compare the enum-cast `$membership->role` with string values via `in_array`/`===`, which always evaluates false; owner/admin can never update or delete an entity, `manageSettings()` always denies the owner, and `assignRole()` always denies owner/admin.

Portability is decided by `$driver === 'mysql'`; Laravel 11+ reports `mariadb` for MariaDB connections, which would take the SQLite trigger path and fail, so the required MariaDB support is not guaranteed.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for the schema, one-owner constraint, models, factories or the policy matrix, so none of the new behavior (including the broken authorization paths) is covered.

The provider extends `Illuminate\Foundation\Providers\AuthServiceProvider`, which is not a framework class (the base is `Illuminate\Foundation\Support\Providers\AuthServiceProvider`), so it would fatal if loaded; it is also never registered, making it dead code that duplicates the Gate::policy calls in AppServiceProvider.
The migrations are hand-written named classes (`class Create... extends Migration`) rather than the anonymous-class files produced by `php artisan make:migration`, which the conventions require.
The role row's 'billing only for owner' rule was deleted even though billing was not part of this change, altering a documented business rule unrelated to the schema fix.
No `[Unreleased]` entry was added for the new tables, models, enum, factories and policies, although conventions require it for every change.

The docblock describes `manageable()` as 'Roles that can manage settings for an entity (i.e., non-owner roles)', which contradicts the owner-only `manageSettings` rule and would mislead future readers.
Entity, EntityMembership, EntityPolicy and EntityMembershipPolicy are imported but the Gate::policy calls still use fully-qualified class names, leaving unused imports.
The removed `owner_membership_id` line was replaced with a whitespace-only line, leaving a malformed gap in the ER diagram.

review.summary: The change adds the entities/entity_memberships migrations, the Entity, EntityMembership and UserRole types, factories, policies and a docs update, but it does not run: User.php has a leftover block that is a parse error, Entity.php imports the wrong SoftDeletes trait, and EntityMembership.php declares UserRole twice (fatal). On top of that the SQLite owner-uniqueness is not implemented with the required generated column and its INSERT trigger is silently dropped, the enum-vs-string policy checks are always false (letting an owner delete their own owner membership), and no tests were added.
